column2: Alteration Lead missing from Acuity sync (Zoia Kozakov)

• SA Sizing Enforcement: Julia wants sizing always entered by the Sales Associate (never determined by the customer alone, since it depends on the exact garment/measurements), with the SA-entered value flowing to Recap — the customer's Acuity size syncs to 'Size From Acuity Intake', and the SA updates the separate 'ready_to_wear_size' field, which is what should feed Recap — done.

Point Recap sizing at the SA-entered ready_to_wear_size field; consolidate notes into one general field; add product-page links to style entries; surface Wedding Date Search on the remaining pages.
column11:
• SA Sizing Enforcement: The sizing workflow did not clearly separate the customer-entered Acuity size from the size confirmed by a Sales Associate. In some interfaces, the editable RTW Size control was tied to the Acuity intake value, while fallback logic elsewhere could still display the customer-entered size when no SA-confirmed value existed. As a result, the system could not reliably guarantee that sizing reaching Recap had been explicitly entered or confirmed by a Sales Associate.

• Recap Doc Product-Page Links: Style entries in the Recap Doc (Favorite, Regular Customization Request, and both styles in a Hybrid Customization Request) had no way to link out to the style's live product page. DF Styles already stored the handle (product_handle_ny), but nothing combined it into an actual URL, and not every style has a handle on file — any implementation needed to omit the link entirely for those, rather than showing a broken one.

• Wedding Date Filtering: Wedding Date filtering was not consistently available across the requested interfaces. Pipeline could support the same filtering pattern already used in Alterations, but Appointments and Recap operate as single-day views: applying a Wedding Date filter on top of the selected appointment day would typically return little or no useful data, since a client’s appointment date is unrelated to their wedding date.
column12:
• SA Sizing Enforcement: Audited all 12 main Daily Ops and Tracking interfaces to standardize sizing behavior. Pipeline, Recap, and Appointments were updated so editable RTW Size inputs write only to the dedicated SA field (ready_to_wear_size_manual), with the Acuity-entered size shown only as a read-only reference when available. Draft Orders was verified to already write to the correct SA field; it was missing that same Acuity reference, which was added. Did Not Convert was corrected to display SA-confirmed sizing with Acuity as reference, after fixing a pre-existing display issue that always left the field blank. The remaining pages do not expose sizing at all and were out of scope. Changes were spot-checked across representative cases.

• Recap Doc Product-Page Links: Added a new formula field, product_page_url, on DF Styles. Each style entry in the Recap Doc now shows a "View [Style Name]" link sourced from this field, styled to match Cobalt's own design reference for this document, scaled to this doc's own typography. Entries whose style has no handle simply show no link — no placeholder, no broken URL.
Separately audited all 704 styles that currently have a handle by checking each resulting URL live: 378 resolve correctly. Of the 325 that don't, 186 are real styles that should have a working page and were compiled into a report for Cobalt to investigate; 139 are internal "-customized" variants.

• Wedding Date Filtering: Implemented and pushed Wedding Date filtering in Pipeline using the existing Alterations pattern. Pipeline filtering was spot-checked against representative Wedding Dates and confirmed to return the expected clients without affecting the existing search and filter behavior. Appointments and Recap require a product decision on whether Wedding Date should search across days or remain out of scope — a question has been submitted to Julia via the Questions/Uncertainty tracker to resolve this.

column2: Date parsing bug - month/day values swapped across interfaces
column3: Month and day values are being swapped in dates shown across the interfaces. Identified live during the Aug 21 joint call. Fix being applied one interface at a time by Axel and Alonso.
column11:
The bug reported as "dates with month/day swapped" turned out to be a family of at least 3 distinct error types, mixed together under the same general symptom, and its scope spans all 11 pages in the system that display, filter, or sort by date: Pipeline, Appointments, Recap, Customization Requests, Alterations, Draft Orders, Sold Orders, Fulfillment, Did Not Convert, Sample Tracker, and Calligraphy Cards.

Type 1 — Genuine month/day swap: a parser that interprets a date string assuming an order (month-first or day-first) different from what the underlying data actually carries, showing a completely wrong date, not just an off-by-a-bit one. Type 2 — ±1-day timezone shift: a time-less date gets converted into a JavaScript date object and read back in the viewer's local time, crossing the midnight boundary of another reference timezone — the experienced effect is that filtering for an exact day returns the next (or previous) day's results, or a record scheduled for "today" gets classified as already past or as "tomorrow," depending on the time and location of whoever is using the tool. This error type can show up as a constant, several-hours-long window every single day for anyone on the team in North America, or only in edge cases (a record whose date falls exactly today or right at a filter's boundary). Type 3 — comparison between incompatible date formats, where the code compares a formatted text string against a standard date value as if they were the same type, producing filtering results with no chronological sense (records silently disappearing from a list or getting miscategorized, with no visible error on screen). Additionally, it was identified that Airtable can, for certain fields, return a native date object (or even an invalid one) instead of a text string — an undocumented behavior that can break any fix that doesn't explicitly account for it.

A sweep of all 11 pages was performed against Airtable's real schema (not just the code's surface appearance), and all 11 require some level of adjustment — none were ruled out outright. However, pinpointing exactly which correction applies on each page requires a deep 1:1 evaluation, since the same error type may or may not be present depending on that specific field's exact usage within that page (e.g., the same field can be handled correctly in its display but incorrectly in its filter, within the same page).
column12: docs/date_handling_rulebook.md was created as the project's source of truth for date handling — it classifies every date value into 5 semantic categories (date-only, date-with-time/instant, formula text with a guaranteed format, free text, and ambiguous human input) and defines 22 normative rules for reading, parsing, comparing, filtering, sorting, and displaying dates, referenced from the project's shared rules document and from the documentation of every affected interface. With that standard now in place, a deep 1:1 evaluation was completed on 2 of the 11 pages: on one, the identified adjustments were confirmed and shipped to production (including the fix for the undocumented Airtable behavior mentioned above); on the other, the specific adjustments were fully diagnosed, pending implementation. Still pending: completing the deep 1:1 evaluation and implementing adjustments on the remaining 9 pages.

column3: Julia's feedback on the waitlist build: make time requested a multi-select of morning, afternoon and evening; make email mandatory as the unique identifier rather than name; add ghost text in notes prompting for style detail or specific times the client needs; capture the appointment type being waitlisted, since waitlists include second and third appointments and alterations, letting the sales associate either tag an existing client or enter a new email. Logic agreed: if a client with the same email books within a week of their earliest available date they drop off the waitlist; if the requested window passes they fade away but are flagged in the backup view. Axel confirmed all points and noted the roughly 95 historical records without an email will not be retroactively cleaned up.

column2: Unique traceable identifier per customization proposal
column3: Julia asked that each customization proposal carry a unique, traceable identifier referenced in the Shopify line-item note, e.g. 'Julia Collins - Ada - August 14th, 2026'. column2: Draft order product naming convention
column3: Regular customizations should use 'Name of Gown - Customized', e.g. 'Ada - Customized'. Hybrid should use the Custom Gown product. Full Custom should use Custom Gown. Answered in response to the dev question about whether a separate Hybrid Gown product needed creating.
